name: Sample size writer
purpose: Writes the sample size section from the scenarios and the sizes computed in code.
prompt:
Agreed focus:
{{focus}}

Scenarios: {{inputs.mlx_power_plan}}
Gate results (the sizes, recruitment figures and any SD limit computed in code are in the sample size check's
items named sizes#<scenario id>, one for each scenario): {{gate_results}}

Write the sample size section. Every sample size, recruitment figure, d and SD limit was computed in code; take
each from that scenario's sizes item exactly (n1, n2 and total are completers; recruit1, recruit2 and
recruit_total are the people to recruit after dropout; sd_used is the SD the d was computed from), and never
compute, round or adjust one yourself. The only numbers you may write are a scenario's stated inputs (alpha,
power and dropout may be written as percentages), the person's own numbers as their request states them, the
figures in those items, the number of scenarios, and years. State no other statistic (a confidence limit, a
variance, an inflation factor) unless an item gives it. Every scenario's total and, where it has dropout, its
recruitment total must appear.
1. For each scenario: the outcome and comparison, the effect size and its basis (a source's citation, where in it
   and its quote), alpha, power, sides and dropout, the completers needed and the people to recruit.
2. The method, named with its source (put each source in the references, cited in square brackets):
   two_means, the normal-approximation formula for two independent means (Chow, Shao and Wang 2008, Sample Size
   Calculations in Clinical Research, 2nd edition, chapter 3); two_proportions, the formula for two independent
   proportions without continuity correction (Fleiss, Levin and Paik 2003, Statistical Methods for Rates and
   Proportions, 3rd edition, chapter 4); logistic_continuous, Hsieh, Bloch and Larsen (1998, Statistics in
   Medicine 17(14), 1623-1634) for one normally distributed predictor, inflated by 1/(1 - r2_other) for the
   other predictors. Recruitment is each arm's completers divided by one minus the dropout rate, rounded up; an
   SD's upper confidence limit is the SD times the square root of (pilot size - 1) over the chi-square quantile.
3. Limits: the normal approximation runs slightly below a t-based calculation for small samples; nothing here
   allows for clustering or repeated measures, so say what the person should add for each that applies.
4. The scenarios as one table, in the first section after its opening sentence, written as a paragraph of its own:
   a Markdown pipe table (every line starts and ends with |; a header row, then a | --- | row, then one row a
   scenario), with the columns Scenario, Effect, SD, Completers per arm, Recruitment per arm and Total to recruit.
   Scenario is its label; Effect its stated effect (d = 0.492, or p1 = 0.30 and p2 = 0.40, or the odds ratio);
   SD the item's sd_used where it gives one, else the scenario's stated SD, else "not used"; per-arm figures as
   "82 and 82" (or "one group"); Total to recruit is recruit_total. Every figure exactly as the scenario or its
   sizes item gives it. Word shows this as a table.

Previous pass (a repair pass only; null on a first pass):
Write-up: {{inputs.draft}}
Failed checks sent back to you: {{gate_results}}
Findings sent back to you: {{findings}}
The person's direction with them: {{inputs.person_direction}}

On a repair pass, fix only what is named, and change nothing else.
Never cite a check's item names or evidence refs in your text (such as sizes#d30_p80, [sizes_d30_p80] or a finding's id): give the figures and facts plainly, in words a reader understands.
